Xiaomi SU7 Xtreme Strips Off Its Camo, Is A New Nürburgring Record Imminent?

MR
By Marco Rossi Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights
  • Looks like the Xtreme is more than just a badge and sticker package China's automakers are in a record-breaking mood.
  • Last week, BYD became the first to smash the 500 kmh barrier with a production car when its Yangwang U9 Xtreme hit 313 mph (503 kmh) on a public highway in Abu Dhabi.
  • Official reporting verified via Carscoops news desk.
⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • MARCO ROSSI Senior Supercar & Aerodynamics Editor

The Benchmark for Track-Tolerant Engineering

In the high-stakes supercar arena, pure horsepower is no longer enough to claim supremacy. This dispatch from Carscoops emphasizes how cutting-edge downforce balance, electronic limited-slip differentials, and hybrid torque-vectoring are reshaping driver engagement. Exotic marques must prove that extreme performance can harmonize with reliability, thermal endurance, and road compliance.

Big Picture: Lap times at benchmark proving grounds and early client allocations will reveal whether this performance envelope disrupts the existing supercar hierarchy.

Looks like the Xtreme is more than just a badge and sticker package

📌 The Core Development

China's automakers are in a record-breaking mood. Last week, BYD became the first to smash the 500 kmh barrier with a production car when its Yangwang U9 Xtreme hit 313 mph (503 kmh) on a public highway in Abu Dhabi. And now it looks like its rival Xiaomi could be about to declare a new EV lap record at Germany's Nürburgring.

Our spy photo team snapped a fully camouflaged SU7 Ultra with a massive GT3-style rear wing putting in some hot laps at the Ring in October, and now another Ultra prototype is busting the same moves, only this time minus the disguise.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Losing the swirly wrap gives us our best look yet at the most aggressive car Xiaomi has made, including all of the other aero parts that complement the big swan-neck rear spoiler. That wing naturally draws your attention, but there's plenty more going on, including a new front bumper, big splitter, and a set of louvers in the front fenders, mounted directly above the wheels. Porsche fits similar parts to the fenders of its 911 GT3 RS to get rid of air pressure that builds up inside the front wheel arches, and it's very likely Xiaomi has the same idea.

And that's not the only GT3 RS idea Xiaomi appears to have appropriated. The SU7's front fenders are cut inwards in front of the door, just like on the hot 911. Likewise, the rear fenders cut inward after the rear wheels, exposing some of the fat trackday rubber wrapped around the double-five-spoke wheels. We'd also be very surprised if that rear wing didn't have some kind of F1-style DRS (drag-reduction system) technology.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

The SU7 did briefly hold the lap record for production sedans and EVs after an Ultra lapped the 12.8-mile (20.6 km) forest track in 7:04.957 in June 2025. That rapid run put it 0.3 seconds ahead of the Rimac Nevera hypercar, and over 2.5 seconds clear of the Porsche Taycan Turbo GT. A massive power advantage was central to Xiaomi's success. The SU7 makes 1,526 hp (1,138 kW / 1,548 PS) for brief periods, but the Taycan's push-to-pass attack mode only gives 939 hp (700 kW / 952 PS).

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

Porsche wasn't about to let an upstart smartphone manufacturer snatch its title and get away with it, though. The German brand returned to the Ring in May of this year with a Taycan Turbo GT modified in conjunction with Manthey . The package included front and rear aero components, road-legal track tires, lighter wheels, and a tweaked bi-motor electric powertrain.

The Manthey Taycan still only makes 978hp (730 kW / 992 PS) in attack mode, which is well below the SU7's output, but that didn't hold the Taycan back. It lapped the Ring in 6:55.553, becoming the first EV and sedan to dip into the sixes. And now it's Xiaomi's turn to reply.
